title: the `dimensionless` marker lands with a gate reader but no docs-generator half — #14478 ruling B put both in the mechanism
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` execution seat, session `session_01KB5PFtxuy1x3dcR5gxudx6`, 2026-09-16T16:2xZ, out of the isolated at-tier contract review of **PR #18486** (card #18123), record `5700807570`, flag **F3** — 「PM to file」. ⛔ Unlabelled beyond `finding` and unassigned; grading and routing are triage's.

## The mechanism is half-built, and the ruling made both halves part of it

PR #18486 adds a **`dimensionless` schema marker** that `check-duration-unit-keys` reads: it lets an author declare, in-schema, that a numeric key counts things rather than measuring time, so the gate stops asking it for a unit. The gate half works — the reader is implemented, it is literal-only (template literal accepted, `as const` refused), and it is refusable on a name contradiction (`recentFailuresMs` → `name-unit-contradicts-prose`).

**The docs half does not exist.** Measured at head:

| marker | renderer in `packages/spec/scripts/lib/schema-section.ts` |
|---|---|
| `externalVocabulary` | **present** — `:256`, prints 「per `<standard>`」 |
| `dimensionless` | **absent** — nothing is printed |

⇒ a key marked `dimensionless` would carry an in-schema declaration that the published reference page says nothing about.

## Why that is the ruling's own requirement, ⛔ not a nicety

#14478 ruling **B**, verbatim:

> declared ON THE SCHEMA, never in a gate ledger … marker the gate honours **and the docs generator publishes**

⇒ 「the docs generator publishes」 is in the ruled sentence. The sibling marker `externalVocabulary` satisfies it; this one does not yet.

## ⛔ This is NOT urgent, and the reason is the useful part

**Population today: 0 keys marked.** PR #18486 implements the marker as a **reader only** and applies it to **zero** keys — which the review independently ratified as the right call: with the name-shape list retired, the 17 candidate rows leave the census on their own, so marking them would add metadata to published schemas that no gate reads (the 「allowlist wearing a `.meta()`」 the script's own header refuses), and would turn a correct `skip-changeset` into a `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` for zero enforcement.

⇒ **the debt is owed before the FIRST key is marked, not before the reader lands.** Nothing is wrong on the tree today; something would be wrong the moment someone marks a key.

## Suggested shape — ⛔ no ruling implied

Add a `dimensionless` arm to `schema-section.ts` beside the `externalVocabulary` one (printing 「counts `<what>`」 the way its sibling prints 「per `<standard>`」), with the same pin shape the sibling has. ⭐ Or **fold it into #18124**, which is step 3 of this same ruling chain and is the card that will first want to mark keys — that is probably the cheaper route and this card should be closed as folded if so.

## ⚠️ One thing NOT measured

`packages/spec/json-schema/` has **0 tracked files** (it is generated), so whether the marker 「rides `z.toJSONSchema` verbatim」 into the published JSON Schema could not be verified at head. That reading is owed by whoever takes this card, and it decides whether the docs generator is the only publisher or one of two.
